title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
title_zh: FrontierPhysics：评估端到端物理学研究的智能体

paragraphs.en: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics , an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents’ research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents’ main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.
paragraphs.zh: AI智能体在物理学研究中正发挥着日益重要的作用。 然而，现有的物理学基准仅评估固定问题、孤立子任务或基于给定解答的论文复现，很少在正确性之外考察研究质量。 我们提出FrontierPhysics，这是一个端到端基准，包含由42位物理学家基于自身研究设计的56个任务，涵盖理论物理、计算物理和实验物理共九个领域。 每个任务要求智能体查阅文献、制定研究计划、开展研究与实验，并产出结构化结果和科学论文。 FrontierPhysics将确定性验证器与专家撰写的评分细则相结合，评估智能体的研究是否正确且具有可发表性。 在26种配置的22个模型中，没有任何配置在其168次 rollout 中通过超过46次。 对智能体轨迹的人工审查表明，前沿智能体的主要弱点是推理不够严谨和专家直觉有限，而非物理知识缺口或执行错误。

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) are evolving from passive scientific assistants into agents that take on parts of the research process. When equipped with external tools, these agents can search and summarize literature, formulate hypotheses, write and debug scientific code, and produce technical reports. Recent systems have demonstrated tool-augmented reasoning in chemistry, iterative code-based experimentation, multi-agent hypothesis generation, scientific-software optimization, and even interaction with laboratory instruments [ 30 , 6 , 29 , 37 , 17 , 4 , 33 , 41 , 20 , 22 , 18 , 31 , 15 ] . These systems point toward agents that contribute to more complete scientific workflows and projects, not only isolated subtasks [ 9 ] .

paragraphs.en: Evaluating progress toward this goal requires benchmarks that capture the open-ended, multi-stage nature of scientific research. Scientific benchmarks are accordingly shifting from textbook-level questions [ 16 , 23 , 48 , 35 , 44 ] toward expert-level closed-ended questions [ 8 ] and research-level problems [ 40 ] . Among existing research-level benchmarks, some assess scientific reasoning [ 10 , 50 , 34 , 25 , 46 ] , while others evaluate the agents’ ability to complete individual tasks within realistic scientific workflows [ 43 , 19 , 31 , 28 , 7 , 21 ] . However, these benchmarks target isolated capabilities, and because many of their tasks are closed-ended with deterministic answers, models quickly saturate them, so the benchmarks lose signal. To move toward end-to-end research, some benchmarks formulate tasks as full-paper reproductions [ 36 , 12 , 49 , 14 ] . Yet because agents are given the original publications, the research questions and solution structures are largely specified in advance, limiting their ability to evaluate open-ended scientific inquiry. More recent benchmarks address this limitation by converting published studies into research problems without revealing their solutions [ 32 , 45 , 47 , 24 ] . Nevertheless, designing and evaluating such tasks involves many subtleties that require the expertise of the original authors: for example, how to write instructions that preserve as much open-endedness as possible while avoiding false negatives, and how to determine if an agent’s failure reflects true scientific misunderstanding or a lack of expert intuition and experience. To our knowledge, no existing benchmark is fully agentic, built by physicists from their own research, graded on both paper quality and result correctness, and designed to address these subtleties through manual task review and failure-mode analysis (Table 1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 评估朝向这一目标的进展需要能够捕捉科学研究开放性、多阶段特点的基准测试。 因此，科学基准测试正从教科书级问题 [ 16 , 23 , 48 , 35 , 44 ] 转向专家级封闭式问题 [ 8 ] 和研究级问题 [ 40 ] 。 在现有的研究级基准测试中，一些评估科学推理能力 [ 10 , 50 , 34 , 25 , 46 ] ，另一些则评估智能体在真实科学工作流中完成单个任务的能力 [ 43 , 19 , 31 , 28 , 7 , 21 ] 。 然而，这些基准测试针对的是孤立的能力，并且由于其许多任务是具有确定性答案的封闭式任务，模型很快就会使其饱和，导致基准测试失去信号。 为了迈向端到端研究，一些基准测试将任务设定为完整论文的复现 [ 36 , 12 , 49 , 14 ] 。 然而，由于智能体被提供了原始出版物，研究问题和解决方案结构在很大程度上已被预先指定，限制了其评估开放式科学探究的能力。 更新的基准测试通过将已发表的研究转化为不披露其解决方案的研究问题来解决这一局限 [ 32 , 45 , 47 , 24 ] 。 尽管如此，设计和评估此类任务涉及许多需要原作者专业知识的微妙之处：例如，如何撰写在尽可能保留开放性的同时避免假阴性的指令，以及如何判断智能体的失败反映的是真正的科学误解，还是缺乏专家直觉与经验。 据我们所知，目前尚无基准测试是完全智能体化的、由物理学家基于自身研究构建、同时依据论文质量和结果正确性进行评分，并通过人工任务审查和失败模式分析来解决上述微妙之处（表 1 ）。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduce FrontierPhysics (Fig. FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research ), a benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can conduct end-to-end research across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. FrontierPhysics tasks are designed by active physics researchers (including Ph.D. students, postdocs, and research scientists) from research projects they have personally conducted. On average, each task author has 420 citations. To preserve open-endedness while minimizing false negatives and positives, each task goes through manual general review, domain-expert peer review, and failure-mode analysis. For each task (Fig. 2 ), an agent receives a high-level prompt that resembles the instructions provided by a principal investigator (PI) at the beginning of a research project. The agent must then carry out the research and produce both a scientific manuscript and numerical outputs that can be verified deterministically. Much of this process is open-ended: the agent must investigate the topic, formulate a research plan, select appropriate methods, validate the results, and establish the significance of its findings. To evaluate these capabilities, FrontierPhysics combines a deterministic verifier (test scripts that check the numerical outputs) with rubric-based grading by reviewer agents.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们介绍 FrontierPhysics（图 FrontierPhysics：评估用于端到端物理学研究的智能体），这是一个评估 AI 智能体能否在理论物理、计算物理和实验物理领域开展端到端研究的基准。 FrontierPhysics 的任务由活跃的物理学研究者（包括博士生、博士后和科研科学家）根据他们亲自开展的研究项目设计。 平均而言，每位任务作者拥有 420 次引用。 为了在保持开放性的同时尽量减少假阴性和假阳性，每项任务都要经过人工总体审查、领域专家同行评审和失效模式分析。 对于每项任务（图 2），智能体会收到一个高层级提示，该提示类似于首席研究员（PI）在研究项目开始时给出的指令。 智能体随后必须开展研究，并产出一份科学手稿以及可以确定性验证的数值输出。 这一过程的很大一部分是开放性的：智能体必须调研该主题、制定研究计划、选择合适的方法、验证结果，并确立其发现的重要性。 为了评估这些能力，FrontierPhysics 将确定性验证器（检查数值输出的测试脚本）与基于评分量表的审稿智能体评分相结合。

paragraphs.en: The rubric-based assessment includes global rubrics and task-specific rubrics. The global rubrics evaluate behavior alignment including reward hacking [ 1 , 38 ] , hallucination and general research practices including literature synthesis, result validation, and the use of evidence to support scientific claims, whereas task-specific rubrics are developed by domain experts to assess the agent’s understanding of the underlying physics, scientific presentation, and execution of the research task. Because rubric design requires task-specific expertise, we ask each contributor to design the rubrics for their own task and research project. Depending on the task, the rubric criteria may assess whether the agent identifies and correctly uses key references, discovers the key scientific ideas through its investigation, considers realistic experimental constraints, or provided good motivations for its work in the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 基于评分标准的评估包括全局评分标准和任务专属评分标准。 全局评分标准评估行为对齐，包括奖励篡改 [ 1 , 38 ] 、幻觉，以及通用科研规范（如文献综合、结果验证和使用证据支持科学论断），而任务专属评分标准由领域专家制定，用于评估智能体对底层物理的理解、科学表达以及研究任务的执行情况。 由于评分标准的设计需要任务相关的专业知识，我们请每位贡献者为自己的任务和研究项目设计评分标准。 视任务而定，评分标准的评估内容可能包括：智能体是否识别并正确使用关键参考文献、是否通过其研究发现了关键科学思想、是否考虑了现实的实验约束条件，或者是否在论文中为其工作提供了充分的动机说明。

sents.en: The rubric-based assessment includes global rubrics and task-specific rubrics.
sents.zh: 基于评分标准的评估包括全局评分标准和任务专属评分标准。

sents.en: The global rubrics evaluate behavior alignment including reward hacking [ 1 , 38 ] , hallucination and general research practices including literature synthesis, result validation, and the use of evidence to support scientific claims, whereas task-specific rubrics are developed by domain experts to assess the agent’s understanding of the underlying physics, scientific presentation, and execution of the research task.
sents.zh: 全局评分标准评估行为对齐，包括奖励篡改 [ 1 , 38 ] 、幻觉，以及通用科研规范（如文献综合、结果验证和使用证据支持科学论断），而任务专属评分标准由领域专家制定，用于评估智能体对底层物理的理解、科学表达以及研究任务的执行情况。

sents.en: Because rubric design requires task-specific expertise, we ask each contributor to design the rubrics for their own task and research project.
sents.zh: 由于评分标准的设计需要任务相关的专业知识，我们请每位贡献者为自己的任务和研究项目设计评分标准。

sents.en: Depending on the task, the rubric criteria may assess whether the agent identifies and correctly uses key references, discovers the key scientific ideas through its investigation, considers realistic experimental constraints, or provided good motivations for its work in the paper.
sents.zh: 视任务而定，评分标准的评估内容可能包括：智能体是否识别并正确使用关键参考文献、是否通过其研究发现了关键科学思想、是否考虑了现实的实验约束条件，或者是否在论文中为其工作提供了充分的动机说明。

paragraphs.en: When a contributor creates a task submission, we first assess its authenticity and provenance (Fig. 3 a): the contributor must provide supporting information (e.g., reference papers or patent links) to demonstrate that they have personally conducted the project. Contributors are asked to provide the project background, a timeline of the original research process, and the amount of time they spent completing it. We require the underlying project to have involved at least two weeks of research effort. We then check that task.md and rubric.json are human-readable and contain genuine human input, rejecting tasks that appear purely AI-generated.
paragraphs.zh: 当贡献者创建任务提交时，我们首先评估其真实性与来源（图 3 a）：贡献者必须提供支持性信息（例如参考文献或专利链接），以证明该课题是由其本人完成的。 我们要求贡献者提供项目背景、原始研究过程的时间线，以及完成该研究所花费的时间。 我们要求底层项目至少涉及两周的研究工作量。 随后我们检查 task.md 和 rubric.json 是否为人类可读，并包含真实的人类输入，拒绝那些看似纯粹由 AI 生成的任务。

paragraphs.en: We aim to have every task reviewed by an expert in a closely related field. To scale this, we invite contributors to become domain reviewers once their own tasks pass the first-stage general quality check. Our domain reviewers have therefore all conducted research in their fields, and consist mostly of Ph.D. students (47%) and Ph.D. holders (37%). Each new reviewer is onboarded through a one-on-one meeting, and we audit the quality of their first review to align standards across reviewers. When a domain reviewer judges a task ready to merge, we perform a final check against our standards.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是让每项任务都由密切相关的领域的专家进行评审。 为了扩大规模，当贡献者自己提交的任务通过第一阶段的质量通审后，我们邀请他们成为领域评审员。 因此，我们的领域评审员都在各自领域开展过研究，主要由博士生（47%）和博士（37%）组成。 每位新评审员都通过一对一会议完成入职培训，并且我们会审核其首次评审的质量，以统一各评审员的标准。 当领域评审员判定某项任务可以合并时，我们会根据我们的标准进行最终检查。

paragraphs.en: Each domain reviewer is provided with a domain-review checklist which covers three aspects: First, the reviewer verifies that task.md does not over-specify the problem: the prompt should not contain domain knowledge that a competent researcher is expected to know or figure out, so that the task remains as open as possible. Second, the reviewer confirms that rubric.json encodes real physics insight that only someone who has conducted the research would possess, rather than the low-signal criteria typical of AI-generated rubrics. Third, the reviewer examines failure modes after getting agents trajectories: contributors must perform at least three local runs with SOTA agents and an initial failure-mode analysis, and the reviewer inspects these traces for finding potential false positives and false negatives. Common issues include unjustified numerical tolerances that fail agents implementing a correct physical model or ambiguous instructions that lead to agents’ misunderstanding.
paragraphs.zh: 每位领域审稿人会收到一份涵盖三个方面的领域审查清单：首先，审稿人核实 task.md 没有对问题过度指定：提示词不应包含有能力的研究者理应知晓或能够自行弄清的领域知识，从而使任务尽可能保持开放性。 其次，审稿人确认 rubric.json 编码了真实的物理洞见，即只有真正开展过该研究的人才会具备的洞见，而不是 AI 生成的评价准则中常见的低信号标准。 第三，审稿人在获取智能体的运行轨迹后检查失效模式：贡献者必须使用 SOTA 智能体进行至少三次本地运行并提供初步的失效模式分析，审稿人会检查这些轨迹以发现潜在的假阳性和假阴性。 常见问题包括：不合理的数值容差导致实现了正确物理模型的智能体失败，或者含糊不清的指令导致智能体产生误解。

paragraphs.en: In each task rollout (Fig. 3 c), our evaluation scheme is designed to assess both the objective correctness of the agent’s results and the overall quality of its research. To this end, we combine programmatic deterministic verifiers with an Agent-as-judge. The deterministic verifier checks structured outputs against reference values. After the agents finish running, agent trajectory files, verifier results, and output files including paper.pdf are recorded and saved. These files are then copied into another sandbox for a reviewer agent to review and grade the trajectory files and paper.pdf based on a rubric.json . We use an agent rather than a single LLM call as the judge because many rubric criteria, such as those on reward hacking, hallucinated results, and literature search, must be checked against the agent’s trajectory, code, and output files rather than paper.pdf alone. All rollouts are graded by the same reviewer agent, GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh) in Codex CLI. Section 3.3 checks its grades against an expert audit (Table 5 , Fig. 6 ) and on the authors’ own papers (Table 11 ). Regrading rollouts of the first evaluation round with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code CLI as the reviewer agent gives the same pass/fail decision for almost all GPT-6 Astra rollouts, but the Opus 5.5 reviewer is more lenient on rollouts from its own model family (Table 6 ). Workspace files and trajectory files of the reviewer agents are collected the same way to HuggingFace datasets for later analysis.
paragraphs.zh: 在每次任务运行（图 3 c）中，我们的评估方案旨在同时评估智能体结果的客观正确性及其研究的整体质量。 为此，我们将程序化确定性验证器与「智能体即裁判」（Agent-as-judge）相结合。 确定性验证器将结构化输出与参考值进行比对检查。 智能体运行结束后，智能体轨迹文件、验证器结果以及包括 paper.pdf 在内的输出文件都会被记录并保存。 这些文件随后会被复制到另一个沙箱中，供一个审稿智能体根据 rubric.json 对轨迹文件和 paper.pdf 进行评审和打分。 我们使用智能体而非单次 LLM 调用作为裁判，是因为许多评分标准，例如关于奖励作弊（reward hacking）、虚构结果和文献检索的标准，必须对照智能体的轨迹、代码和输出文件来检查，而不能仅依据 paper.pdf。 所有运行均由同一个审稿智能体打分，即 Codex CLI 中的 GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh)。 第 3.3 节将其评分与专家审计（表 5、图 6）以及作者本人的论文（表 11）进行了对照检验。 使用 Claude Code CLI 中的 Claude Opus 5.5 作为审稿智能体对第一轮评估的运行结果重新打分，对于几乎所有 GPT-6 Astra 的运行给出了相同的通过/未通过判定，但 Opus 5.5 审稿者对其自身模型家族的运行更为宽松（表 6）。 审稿智能体的工作区文件和轨迹文件以同样的方式收集到 HuggingFace 数据集中，供后续分析使用。

paragraphs.en: Rubric-based grading has been widely adopted in benchmarks involving open-ended exploration or qualitative dimensions of agent performance [ 39 , 3 , 13 , 36 , 11 ] . Whereas deterministic verification establishes whether an output is correct, rubric-based evaluation assesses more aspects, for example whether the agent conducted and communicated the research well. Inspired by the rubric design of FrontierCode [ 11 ] , we divide our rubric criteria into blockers and non-blockers . Blockers are binary gates that represent requirements essential to the scientific validity of a task. Thus, an agent must satisfy every blocker as well as the deterministic verifier to pass. Non-blockers capture qualitative aspects of the work. Each non-blocker is scored on a three-level scale: 0 indicates that the requirement is absent or incorrect, 1 indicates partial satisfaction, and 2 indicates complete satisfaction. The precise anchors for these levels are defined separately for each criterion. The task author also gives every criterion an integer weight from 1 to 10 for its relative importance. paragraphs.en: First, we ask every task contributor to do a failure-mode report of the three GPT-6 Astra rollouts, as this is the best performing model with single agent harness when the analysis started, check the agent trajectories and output files, and explain where the agent failed and why. Second, our admin team reviewers re-read these contributors’ failure-mode reports and double check them against the agent trajectories and output files. After reviewing around 60 rollouts, reviewers consolidated the recurring failures into the taxonomy in Table 4 . False negatives, where agents deliver the correct results but failed by verifier or reviewer agent, are found during this process and are labeled in Appendix E . As highlighted in Table 5 , rollouts with exclusively false failures lead to an underestimated pass rate. In total, nine of the 168 rollouts incorrectly failed. This coincides with the recent research [ 2 ] , in which domain experts regrade some leading benchmarks and find that many failures are due to grader errors, incorrect reference solutions, and ambiguous or underspecified questions. This suggests that finding false negatives takes both domain expertise and time, but is crucial for maintaining high benchmark quality.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，我们要求每位任务贡献者对三次 GPT-6 Astra 推演进行失败模式报告，因为在分析开始时，它是配合单智能体框架表现最好的模型，查看智能体轨迹和输出文件，并解释智能体在哪里失败以及为什么失败。 其次，我们的管理团队评审员重新阅读这些贡献者的失败模式报告，并对照智能体轨迹和输出文件进行复核。 在评审了约 60 次推演后，评审员将反复出现的失败归纳为表 4 中的分类体系。 假阴性（即智能体给出了正确结果却被验证器或评审智能体判定为失败）就是在此过程中被发现，并标注在附录 E 中。 如表 5 所强调，仅包含假性失败的推演会导致通过率被低估。 总共，168 次推演中有 9 次被错误地判定为失败。 这与近期研究 [ 2 ] 相吻合，该研究让领域专家对一些领先的基准进行重新评分，发现许多失败是由于评分器错误、参考解答错误以及问题含糊或说明不足。 这表明发现假阴性既需要领域专业知识又需要时间，但对于保持基准的高质量至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Figure 6 shows that agents mostly do not fail because of physics mistakes (e.g., a wrong calculation, misunderstanding of the physics concepts or lacking of physics knowledge), contrary to what one might expect from a physics benchmark. Instead, they often struggle to reason rigorously (48%), apply good physical intuition when making decisions (34%), and synthesize the literature (27%). Typical rigorous thinking failures are: circular self-verification, where the agent’s own validation method depends on its wrong assumption, so it can never find out its mistakes; and edge cases, where the agent fails to consider all the edge cases of its method or code, so that it fails at some hidden tests. The third most frequent failure is in the literature. In many cases, agents fail to find the key literature for the research (as identified by the task author), struggle to synthesize information from its literature search and provide a motivation for its project, or struggle to support its argument in the manuscript with literature. Missing physics intuition is another major failure mode. Typical examples of this failure mode include: agents fail to determine the major error source of an experiment, which is not because they do not understand it, but because they do not have the expert intuition to identify what is important; when debugging, agents cannot realize the root of the problem while keeping tuning the wrong knob. Besides the top three failure modes, instruction following accounts for 26% of the failures. It could be agents missing some requirements in the instructions or misunderstanding the instructions. In many cases, the task authors believe the meaning should be clear to human domain experts, while the agent cannot get the explicit/implicit message.
paragraphs.zh: 图6表明，智能体大多并非因为物理错误（例如计算错误、对物理概念的误解或缺乏物理知识）而失败，这与人们通常对物理基准测试的预期相反。 相反，它们常常难以进行严谨推理（48%）、在决策时运用良好的物理直觉（34%），以及综合文献（27%）。 典型的严谨思维失败包括：循环自我验证，即智能体自身的验证方法依赖于其错误假设，因此永远无法发现自己的错误；以及边缘情况，即智能体未能考虑其方法或代码的所有边缘情况，从而在某些隐藏测试中失败。 第三常见的失败出现在文献方面。 在许多情况下，智能体未能找到研究所需的关键文献（由任务作者认定），难以综合其文献检索所得的信息并为项目提供动机，或者难以用文献支持稿件中的论点。 缺乏物理直觉是另一种主要的失败模式。 这一失败模式的典型例子包括：智能体无法确定实验的主要误差来源，这并非因为它们不理解，而是因为它们缺乏识别什么才是重要因素的专家直觉；在调试时，智能体意识不到问题的根源，却不断调整错误的旋钮。 除了这三大失败模式之外，指令遵循占失败原因的26%。 这可能是智能体遗漏了指令中的某些要求，或者误解了指令。 在许多情况下，任务作者认为其含义对人类领域专家而言应当是明确的，而智能体却无法获取其中显性或隐性的信息。

paragraphs.en: We have introduced FrontierPhysics , a benchmark dataset with 56 tasks evaluating the ability of AI agents to conduct physics research across nine domains. FrontierPhysics shows end-to-end physics research remains challenging to current models, given that Opus 5.5 in Claude Code CLI, the configuration with the highest pass rate, passes only 46 of its 168 rollouts. Based on the human experts auditing of 168 SOTA agents rollouts trajectory and output files, we build a failure mode taxonomy and label all these 168 rollouts manually. From the taxonomy distribution, we conclude that lack of rigorous thinking (for example, circular self-verification) followed by missing expert intuition, instead of insufficient physics knowledge or execution mistakes, are the main weaknesses of frontier LLM agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出了 FrontierPhysics，一个包含 56 个任务的基准数据集，用于评估 AI 智能体在九个领域开展物理学研究的能力。 FrontierPhysics 表明，端到端的物理学研究对当前模型而言仍然具有挑战性，因为通过率最高的配置——Claude Code CLI 中的 Opus 5.5——在其 168 次 rollout 中也仅通过了 46 次。 基于人类专家对 168 条 SOTA 智能体的 rollout 轨迹和输出文件的审计，我们构建了一个失败模式分类体系，并对全部 168 次 rollout 进行了人工标注。 从分类体系的分布来看，我们得出结论：缺乏严谨的思考（例如循环式自我验证）以及缺失专家直觉，而非物理知识不足或执行失误，是前沿 LLM 智能体的主要弱点。

paragraphs.en: Capable physics research agents should go beyond specified tasks to explore scientific problems independently, from problem definition to novel findings, with only high-level guidance. Training and evaluating such agents will require more open-ended research tasks and flexible evaluation frameworks that can assess exploratory reasoning, partial progress, and unexpected findings.
paragraphs.zh: 有能力完成物理研究的智能体应当在仅接受高层指导的情况下，超越指定任务，独立地探索科学问题，从问题定义到取得新发现。 训练和评估这类智能体将需要更加开放的研究任务以及灵活的评估框架，以便能够评估探索性推理、阶段性进展和意外发现。

paragraphs.en: Agent time is the recorded execution-stage wall-clock duration, excluding environment setup, verification and rubric review. When an idle-timeout record lacks that stage timer, its recorded elapsed execution time supplies the duration. Agent steps count recorded tool invocations, including failed and interrupted calls. A partial trace is used only when a termination monitor supplies a tool-call counter. Output tokens use the reported agent output-token count; unavailable usage records are omitted. Tokenization and output-token accounting can differ between providers. In Claude Code runs, agent time and steps include subagent work.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体时间是指记录的执行阶段实际耗时，不包括环境设置、验证和评分规则审查。 当空闲超时记录缺少该阶段计时器时，其记录的实际执行耗时将作为时长。 智能体步数统计记录的工具调用次数，包括失败和被中断的调用。 部分轨迹仅在终止监控器提供工具调用计数器时使用。 输出 token 使用报告的智能体输出 token 数；不可用的用量记录将被省略。 不同提供商之间的 token 化和输出 token 统计可能存在差异。 在 Claude Code 运行中，智能体时间和步数包括子智能体的工作。

sents.zh: 智能体步数统计记录的工具调用次数，包括失败和被中断的调用。

sents.en: A partial trace is used only when a termination monitor supplies a tool-call counter.
sents.zh: 部分轨迹仅在终止监控器提供工具调用计数器时使用。

sents.en: Output tokens use the reported agent output-token count; unavailable usage records are omitted.
sents.zh: 输出 token 使用报告的智能体输出 token 数；不可用的用量记录将被省略。

sents.en: Tokenization and output-token accounting can differ between providers.
sents.zh: 不同提供商之间的 token 化和输出 token 统计可能存在差异。

sents.en: In Claude Code runs, agent time and steps include subagent work.
